FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.

2. When practising Critical Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening.

3. When practising Persuasive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive Speaking.

4. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Thank you
   C. Good morning / hello
   D. Good night only

5. When practising Intensive Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.

6. When practising Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

7. When practising Interactive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Interactive speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive speaking.

8. When practising Informative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Informative Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Informative Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Informative Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.

9. When practising Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

10. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. chaise
   B. porte
   C. fenêtre
   D. livre

11. When practising Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading.

12. When practising Reading for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading for information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading for information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for information.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Language structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Critical Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

2. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening.

3. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive Speaking.

4. C — Good morning / hello

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Listening.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Language structures ● Lang.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Informative Speaking.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing ● Descriptive writing ● Expository writing ● Descriptive writing ● Proce.

10. D — livre

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading.

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for information.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Language structures; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Critical Listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for Information; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
